rationale: Targeted check of the 4 prior blocking findings against current source: all resolved (handler annotated, helper typed dict[str, Any], gate compares header and explicit values with lower() matching the lookup and no strip/casefold, migration test pins only its parent revision). No new findings were discovered by design; business_review and standards_review are carried forward unchanged from the final round.

standards_review.notes: 7 subjects in diff_base..HEAD all match the documented 'EPMCDME-####: Description' format
Two type-hint rules unmet in new code: bare dict in crud.py _with_visible_cli_analytics; unannotated handler in project.py _omit_cli_analytics_when_hidden.
Gate fails closed and write paths are guarded; ingest gate strips and casefolds project values before the conflict decision (security-patterns 'Untrusted Input Handling').

findings.title: Annotate serializer handler parameter
findings.problem: code-quality.md says not to leave a duck-typed parameter unannotated; _omit_cli_analytics_when_hidden(self, handler) has an unannotated 'handler' and a deliberately omitted return type.
findings.impact: Documented Types And Imports standard is not met in newly added code.
findings.recommendation: Annotate handler as pydantic.SerializerFunctionWrapHandler; keep (and justify in the comment) the omitted return annotation that preserves the OpenAPI schema.

findings.title: Parameterize dict annotations on visibility helper
findings.problem: code-quality.md prefers parameterized generics over bare dict annotations; new helper _with_visible_cli_analytics is declared '(user: User, project: dict) -> dict'.
findings.impact: Documented Types And Imports standard is not met in newly added code.
findings.recommendation: Annotate both the parameter and the return value as dict[str, Any].

findings.title: Gate normalizes project values before deciding
findings.problem: build_ingest_gate strips the header project and strips plus casefolds every explicit body project value before the conflict comparison, and _note_project in postgres/otlp.py strips values before they reach the gate; security-patterns.md 'Untrusted Input Handling' says to parse input exactly as received and avoid stripping or silent coercion before a security decision. The conflict check uses casefold() while the policy lookup (aget_by_name_case_insensitive) compares lower(), so the two disagree for some strings (e.g. 'ss' vs 'ß').
findings.impact: A body project value that differs from the header only by whitespace or case is treated as the same project and the request is stored, while the stored attribute stays unnormalized; the conflict decision and the policy lookup can disagree on what counts as the same project. Reachability confirmed: all four ingest endpoints route through this gate.
findings.recommendation: Compare header and explicit values exactly as received and look up with that same value, dropping the strip/casefold from the conflict check; if case-insensitive matching is intentional, use the same lower() as the lookup in both places and document the exception. The exact-vs-case-insensitive choice is ambiguous and is the author's to settle.

findings.title: Migration test pins itself as the alembic head
findings.problem: test_revision_is_the_single_alembic_head asserts script.get_heads() == [module.revision], so it is true only while this migration is the newest one in the alembic directory.
findings.impact: The test fails as soon as any later migration lands on top, or on a merge with another branch that adds a migration (the branch already shares files with EPMCDME-14659), producing a red CI unrelated to this migration's correctness.
findings.recommendation: Drop the get_heads equality; assert only that module.revision exists in the script directory and that its down_revision is 'y1z2a3b4c5d6'.
